trestolone-ment.text: On looksmax forums trestolone is discussed as a topical androgen that might remodel the jawline and face, alongside DHT and trenbolone, and as a far stronger anabolic than testosterone for muscle. The facial remodeling idea is based on theory and anecdote; it was studied as a male contraceptive and replacement androgen.

dimethandrolone-undecanoate.text: Forum users speculate that DMAU could become an oral anabolic steroid, since it is a potent androgen taken by mouth. It was developed as a male contraceptive pill and androgen replacement; trials looked at hormone levels and safety, and its effect on muscle or looks in healthy users is untested.

methasterone.text: Sold in the 2000s as Superdrol, methasterone is used by bodybuilders for quick lean muscle gain with little water retention, and some posters claim non-aromatizing steroids add height in teenagers. Its muscle effect rests on user reports and its androgen class; no human trial exists, and the height claim is untested.

androstenedione.text: Marketed in the 1990s as a testosterone-booster prohormone, androstenedione is taken by users hoping to convert it into testosterone and build muscle. Trials at ordinary oral doses looked at strength and muscle gains and did not find them; relabelled analogues such as 1-andro followed after bans.

dhea.text: DHEA is taken as a fountain-of-youth supplement for skin and vitality, as a way to raise testosterone, and in some forum posts for height. It is well studied for vaginal atrophy; its use for skin, muscle, or growth in healthy people has thin evidence and rests largely on anecdote.

chain: Local facial bone and tissue effect
dihydrotestosterone-dht.text: DHT gel is promoted on forums for masculinizing the face during puberty, strengthening the jaw, and increasing penile size. DHT is the androgen that drives facial and body hair at puberty, but the facial bone and size claims for applied gel are anecdotal, with no trials in healthy people.

human-chorionic-gonadotropin-hcg.text: Men on testosterone therapy use hCG to keep the testes active and preserve fertility, and some looksmaxxers add it to growth hormone or DHT gel hoping for facial or penile growth. Its testicular use is established medically; the facial, height, and size claims are untested.

andarine-s-4.text: Andarine is a SARM that users take during cutting phases to hold onto muscle while losing fat, with posters saying it spares hair compared with steroids. Evidence for that use comes from animal studies and anecdote, and users also report a yellow-green tint to vision.

cardarine-gw501516.text: Cardarine is used as a fat-loss and endurance aid, often described as a milder alternative to clenbuterol for getting lean. Small trials looked at lipid and metabolic markers rather than appearance, and development stopped after rodent cancer findings.

sr9009-stenabolic.text: Sold as Stenabolic, SR9009 is used for endurance and cutting, often stacked with cardarine and other compounds. The fat-loss and endurance effects come from mouse studies; human appearance data is absent, and it is not actually a SARM despite being sold alongside them.

cjc-1295-with-dac.text: CJC-1295 with DAC is a long-acting GHRH analogue used in growth hormone peptide stacks, with users aiming for better body composition, recovery, and skin. Forum posters debate combining it with ipamorelin or preferring the no-DAC version. Its effects on appearance have not been tested in trials.

modified-grf-1-29.text: Mod GRF (CJC-1295 without DAC) is paired with a GHRP in forum stacks to boost growth hormone pulses, with users citing better sleep, recovery, and body composition. The synergy is described in hormone studies; human trials for appearance are absent.

ghrp-2-pralmorelin.text: GHRP-2 is used by peptide users to raise growth hormone for muscle growth, recovery, sleep, and sometimes height, and is preferred to GHRP-6 for causing less hunger. It is a real diagnostic agent in Japan; evidence that it builds muscle or height in healthy users is lacking.

hexarelin-examorelin.text: Hexarelin is regarded in peptide circles as the most potent GH-releasing peptide, used alone or with a GHRH analogue to build muscle with less water retention. It was studied in 1990s endocrine trials for hormone release; appearance effects are untested, and desensitization with repeated use is discussed.

bimagrumab.text: Bimagrumab is an investigational antibody that blocks activin receptors, and appearance communities follow it as a way to lose fat while preserving or adding muscle. Trials report fat loss with muscle preservation in people with obesity; it is not available outside studies.

survodutide.text: Survodutide is a once-weekly injectable followed by people interested in the next generation of weight-loss peptides. Phase 2 and 3 trials in obesity and fatty liver disease report weight loss, and it has not been approved; appearance effects arrive through fat loss.

vk2735.text: VK2735 is an investigational GLP-1/GIP agonist watched by people seeking strong fat loss. Phase 2 reported roughly 9 to 15 percent weight loss in 13 weeks, and phase 3 is underway. Its effect on appearance comes through reduced body fat.

cagrisema.text: CagriSema is a weekly cagrilintide and semaglutide shot discussed by users chasing large fat loss, sometimes compared with retatrutide. Phase 3 trials showed weight loss of about 20 percent in people with obesity. It is not approved, and any effect on looks comes through fat loss.

exenatide.text: Exenatide, the original GLP-1 shot, is mentioned by users as an early route to appetite control and fat loss, now overshadowed by semaglutide. Trials in type 2 diabetes show modest weight loss; its use for appearance is off-label.

tesofensine.text: Tesofensine is promoted for strong appetite suppression and fat loss, and some users see it as an alternative to approved weight-loss drugs. A 24-week trial found weight loss beyond placebo of about 4.5 to 10.6 percent, with raised heart rate and blood pressure. It is not approved.

orlistat.text: Orlistat is used during cutting phases to absorb less dietary fat, and some describe it as a replacement for banned stimulants. Trials show a few kilos of weight loss over placebo, with oily stools as a known effect; it works less for people already eating low-fat.

naltrexone-bupropion-contrave.text: Contrave is a prescription pill used for appetite control and weight management, followed by people seeking fat loss without injections. Trials show solid but modest weight loss compared with GLP-1 drugs. Its appearance effect comes through reduced body fat.

phentermine.text: Phentermine is a decades-old prescription appetite suppressant used for short-term weight loss and cutting. Trials show modest weight loss over a few weeks to months, and it appears in many forum fat-loss stacks. The appearance effect comes through reduced body fat.

phentermine-topiramate-qsymia.text: Qsymia is a once-daily capsule used for chronic weight management and discussed as a non-injection route to fat loss. Trials show clear weight loss over placebo, though less than GLP-1 injections. Its appearance effect comes through reduced body fat.

clenbuterol.text: Clenbuterol is a gray-market cutting pill, said to give a shredded look, increase vascularity, and sometimes stacked with DNP. It was developed as an asthma drug, and a 1995 review noted athletes' use for purported fat loss and anabolic effects. Human evidence for those effects is limited.

2-4-dinitrophenol-dnp.text: DNP is used by some bodybuilders as a fast cutting drug, with users reporting around 8 to 10 lb of fat loss in three weeks. It raises metabolic rate by uncoupling cells' energy production and was sold as a diet drug in the 1930s. Posters compare it with GLP-1 options.

ephedrine.text: Ephedrine is the stimulant in the classic ECA stack, used for appetite suppression and energy during fasted cardio while cutting. Trials show modest fat loss, and it is a milder thermogenic than clenbuterol or DNP. Forum users also pair it with MK-677 to offset hunger.

sibutramine.text: Sibutramine is a withdrawn appetite suppressant that cutting forum users see as a substitute or complement to an ECA stack. Randomised trials found modest weight loss beyond diet and exercise. Its appearance effect comes through reduced body fat.

ketoconazole.text: Ketoconazole shampoo (Nizoral) is added to finasteride and minoxidil routines in hair-loss communities for less shedding and a cleaner, calmer scalp, alongside its use for dandruff. Small studies hint at benefit for pattern hair loss; large trials are missing.

baricitinib.text: Baricitinib is a prescription JAK inhibitor approved for severe alopecia areata, an autoimmune condition causing patchy or total hair loss. It is followed in hair communities for its regrowth results, and it is not approved for ordinary male pattern baldness.
